question.:question/problem: The slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}$ at the point where $x=3$ is{{field-1}}.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=2{x}^{2}+6x.$ Then $y=\sqrt{u}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}},
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=4x+6.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (4x+6) \\  & =\frac{2(2x+3)}{2\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}} \\  & =\frac{2x+3}{\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, substituting $x=3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=3} & ={(\frac{2x+3}{\sqrt{2{x}^{2}+6x}})|}_{x=3} \\  & =\frac{4(3)+6}{2\sqrt{2(3{)}^{2}+6(3)}} \\  & =\frac{18}{2\sqrt{36}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=-2x-4.

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =-\frac{1}{2\sqrt{{u}^{3}}}\cdot (-2x-4) \\  & =\frac{2x+4}{2\sqrt{(-{x}^{2}-4x{)}^{3}}}.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: Find the slope of the tangent to the curve $y=\sqrt{3x+45}-2{x}^{3}$ at the point where $x=-3.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
To find the slope at a given point, we have to find $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}$ at that point.

Let $f(x)=\sqrt{3x+45}.$ We use the chain rule in the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x}=\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}.
$$

Let $u=3x+45.$ Then $f=\sqrt{u}={u}^{1/2}.$ Differentiating, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{2}{u}^{-1/2}=\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}
$$

and

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=3.
$$

Multiplying the two together gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{1}{2\sqrt{u}}\cdot (3) \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{u}} \\  & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3x+45}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the sum rule, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3x+45}}-6x^{2}.
$$

Finally, substituting $x=-3,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=-3} & =\frac{3}{2\sqrt{3(-3)+45}}-6(-3)^{2} \\  & =\frac{1}{4}-54 \\  & =-\frac{215}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$
